The PRD may not advance to `ready` until review_rounds >= 1.

tables: attempts (joined to calls for per-seat latency and outcome_kind)

not_read_and_flagged: `claude -p` was never executed -- the permission gate refused it in the authoring session. The ~7,500-token harness figure rests on ONE stored usage record plus the argv. The confront then established something sharper: NEITHER CLI argv forwards any output-token limit (cli.py:114 and :344), so seat.max_output_tokens reaches no CLI child. Task t8 must establish a verified effective cap and a documented mechanism, and force singles until it has one.

the per-item payload/output size for the critic role is unmeasured (its prompt carries ballots and votes, so it is larger than the proposer's ~1,200 chars); batch size is derived at runtime, so this does not block the build
individual test bodies under tests/domains/ai/council/ -- the listing was used to identify test shape only

design_changing_stalls: seat names do not bind to one account -- roster() overrides can replace the whole proposer bench, so account validation must cover every declared profile
a shared store lock alone does not stop two configs over-committing a provider -- queue workers now run only under a single controller with an immutable config
NO CLI argv forwards an output-token limit at all, so the batch ceiling divided by an unenforced number; batching now requires a verified cap or falls back to singles

decisions_settled_in_session.partition_key: seat for the queue, account for the budget -- confirmed explicitly by Chris 2026-10-19T18:40Z
decisions_settled_in_session.batch_size: QueueConfig.batch_size defaults to 1 and accepts 1-50; 20 is the recommended explicit opt-in for a Claude queue. Chris proposed ~50, then observed 20 already reduces overheads significantly, and the 7500/n+300 curve agrees (11.6x of a maximum 21x). CORRECTED after confront stall 3: an earlier wording said '20 by default', which contradicted the declared default of 1 and would have changed existing spend on upgrade.
